sections.h2: What two certificates does a Sayreville house need before closing?
sections.html:
A Sayreville seller needs a Certificate of Residential Resale Compliance from the borough and a separate smoke, carbon monoxide and secondary power source certificate from the Bureau of Fire Prevention. The fire marshal's 2026 sheet says the second one is required for closing regardless of the house's condition or any as-is terms in the contract.

Sayreville had 45,345 residents in 2020, an estimate of 46,787 for July 2025, and 15.83 square miles of land. It sits on the south bank of the Raritan River in Middlesex County and also touches Raritan Bay.

sections.h2: How do you book the Sayreville resale inspection?
sections.html:
The borough runs resale applications online. You create an account, fill in the application, submit it, and the office emails the fee, usually within one business day. After you pay online you request an appointment, and resale inspections are held on Mondays and Wednesdays, while rental inspections use Tuesdays and Thursdays.

Questions go to the Code Enforcement contact at 732-390-7077. The borough asks owners and agents to call as soon as the house is listed so the office can check the file for open permits. The inspector looks for recently installed water heaters, furnaces and finished basements, and a permit that was never closed out can hold a certificate.

The Bureau of Fire Prevention is at 167 Main Street and can be reached at 732-390-7009 for the alarm inspection.

sections.h2: What does the Sayreville resale checklist cover?
sections.html:
The borough's checklist has 20 items, and violations bring a correction notice and a reinspection before the certificate is released. Inspectors may also cite other violations of the International Property Maintenance Code and borough ordinances.

  • Exit doors must open from inside without a key, and double-keyed deadbolts are prohibited.
  • Stairs with three or more steps need a handrail, and house numbers must be at least 4 inches tall and visible from the street.
  • Kitchen stoves need anti-tip devices, and a single-family house may have only one working kitchen.
  • A basement, attic or garage used as a bedroom must meet habitable-space rules, including an approved egress window that needs a construction permit, or the house fails.
  • Pools deeper than 18 inches need a fence at least 48 inches high with a self-closing, self-latching gate.
  • The water curb stop must work, and the Water Department at 732-390-7060 should be called before closing.

The checklist states that houses sold as-is are not exempt from permit requirements, and that a New Jersey licensed contractor must apply for and finalize any missing permits.

sections.h2: What are Sayreville's alarm and labeling rules?
sections.html:
Alarms go on every finished level, within 10 feet of each sleeping area, at the bottom of basement stairs, and in finished attics with 7 feet or more of ceiling height. Smoke alarms must be under 10 years old, and stand-alone battery units must be 10-year sealed. Carbon monoxide alarms must be under 7 years old. Devices that are part of a home security system do not count and need stand-alone units beside them.

Since February 3, 2025, a house with solar panels, battery storage or a generator must display a printed label reading "CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER," fixed within 18 inches of the main panel and the meter. Handwritten labels are rejected. Portable fire extinguishers are no longer required for resale inspections, and the fire marshal asks owners to drop old ones at a Middlesex County household hazardous waste day.

sections.html:

The borough has 17,187 households averaging 2.66 people, and 41.4 percent of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home. Median household income is $99,979, and 36.6 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

The 2020 census found 17,695 housing units, 4.4 percent of them vacant, with a rental vacancy rate of 6.2 percent and a homeowner vacancy rate of 1.2 percent. The median age was 40.1, and 21.0 percent of residents were under 18. Sayreville has a skate park in Kennedy Park and the Starland Ballroom concert venue, which opened in December 2003.

sections.h2: What shaped Sayreville, and what does flooding mean for a house here?
sections.html:
The area was called Roundabout, then Wood's Landing, and was renamed in the 1860s for James R. Sayre Jr., co-founder of the Sayre and Fisher Brick Company. Brick-making on local clay lasted until 1970 and reached 6.2 billion bricks over the company's first century. DuPont began making gunpowder here in 1898, and in 1918 explosions at the Gillespie Shell Loading Plant killed dozens and damaged hundreds of buildings. Sayreville became a township in 1876 and a borough on April 2, 1919.

Low-lying ground near the river floods in storm surges. After Hurricane Sandy in 2012, residents accepted a federally funded offer in 2013 to buy out 250 floodplain houses. A seller near the water should gather any flood insurance and elevation records, since buyers will ask. The borough's recorded hot-weather extreme is 110 degrees in Runyon on July 10, 1936, the state record.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods, roads and schools define Sayreville?
sections.html:
Named sections include Crossmans, Ernston, Gillespie, Laurel Park, MacArthur Manor, Melrose, Morgan, Morgan Heights, Phoenix, Runyon, Sayre Woods, Sayreville Junction and Sayreville Station. The borough uses four ZIP codes, 08871, 08872, 08879 and 08859, so check the one on your deed and tax record.

The Garden State Parkway crosses the Raritan on the Driscoll Bridge, 15 lanes wide. U.S. Route 9 uses the Edison Bridge, and Route 35 uses the Victory Bridge to Perth Amboy. Of the borough's 130.58 miles of roadway, 101.75 are municipal. NJ Transit buses 131 and 139 run to Port Authority, the 67 to Newark and the 64 to Jersey City.

Sayreville Public Schools had nine schools and 6,407 students in 2022 to 2023, with Sayreville War Memorial High School at 1,750. The Riverton redevelopment of the former National Lead site, a $2.5 billion mixed-use plan, lists a Bass Pro Shops as an anchor and is one of the largest brownfield projects in the state.

sections.h2: What costs and tax steps apply to a Sayreville sale?
sections.html:
Middlesex County's Board of Taxation is at 75 Bayard Street, fourth floor, New Brunswick, phone 732-745-3350, and takes petitions through an online portal. Its added or omitted assessment deadline is December 1. Ask the board for the regular filing date for Sayreville.

At the borough's $444,100 median value, the state transfer fee comes to about $3,638 when each band's rate is applied to the slice of price inside it. A corporation, partnership or multi-member LLC signs a GIT/REP-3 and checks box 5, and an individual out-of-state seller pays at least 2 percent of the deed price in estimated tax unless an assurance applies.

faqs.q: What is the Sayreville Certificate of Residential Resale Compliance?
faqs.a: It is the borough's clearance after an inspection against a 20-item checklist covering life safety, interior conditions, building systems, exterior conditions and permits. It is separate from the fire marshal's alarm certificate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sayreville house as-is without these inspections?
faqs.a: No. The fire marshal's sheet says the alarm certificate is required for closing despite any as-is terms, and the borough checklist says as-is houses are not exempt from permit requirements.

faqs.q: On which days are Sayreville resale inspections held?
faqs.a: Mondays and Wednesdays. Rental inspections are on Tuesdays and Thursdays. You request a date after paying the emailed fee online.

faqs.q: Do I need a fire extinguisher for the Sayreville inspection?
faqs.a: No. Since February 3, 2025, state law no longer requires one for resale inspections. Solar, battery or generator systems need a printed power-source warning label instead.
Parts are. Low ground along the Raritan River floods in storm surges, and after Hurricane Sandy 250 houses in the floodplain were bought out under a federally funded offer in 2013.
